why: Rung 4 (a proof whose bytes moved since its ladder opened needs Akien's ruling) is checked only in the reseal door (cairn/devices/tester/reseal.py:329, read_ladder's sole consumer). Plain `cairn test --seal` never reads the ladder: it writes a new standing record with no reseal_ladder, so the bound vanishes and read_ladder returns None afterwards. Measured 2026-10-08 on cairn/tools/scratch/proofs/test_scratch.py: the pre-commit reseal of 21961d19 printed RUNG 4 REFUSED (ladder opened 2026-10-08T04:46:05 bounding proof_sha256 1dd04adaaf27..., file now 5072123bd7ba...; 'Refused: no ruling id was given'); the committed seal at 21961d19 carries that ladder; b4d39f3610f3's D13 step then ran `bin/cairn test --seal` on the same proof, and the committed seal at c3ef0d02 carries ladder None. This time a covering answer existed (open-637f083600aa, answered by Akien, naming this proof's edit), but nothing checked it. The commit-level print is by design (hook: `--reseal --stage || true`, 'WHY THE RESEAL NEVER BLOCKS'), so the defect is the second door, not the hook.
